summary:
Walk the text with two pointers: `i` at the start of a run, `j` advancing while the character repeats. Append
the character and, if the run is longer than 1, its length. Then jump `i` to `j`. O(n) with a string builder.

question.md:
Replace each run of a repeated character with the character followed by the run length; runs of length 1 are
just the character. `"aaabcc"` → `"a3bc2"`.

- **Lengths can have several digits** (a run of 12 becomes `a12`).
- **Up to 10⁵ characters.**

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Runs of length 1 are written without a number.
- Long runs need multi-digit counts (`a12`).
- The whole text can be one run, or every character can be its own run.

think.md:
**Runs with two pointers.** `i` marks the start of a run. Move `j` right while `text[j]` equals `text[i]`; when
it stops, the run is `text[i .. j)` with length `j − i`. Emit the character (and the length if it's more than 1),
then start the next run at `j`.

Result **`a3bc2d4x`**.

**Building the output efficiently.** Appending to a string with `+` in a loop can copy the whole result every
time, which is O(n²) overall in some languages. Collect pieces in a list (Python), a `StringBuilder` (Java), a
`string` with `+=` (C++, which appends in place), or write into a preallocated buffer (C).

approaches.title: Two pointers over runs

idea.md:
Walk the runs with `i` and `j` as above, appending each run's code to an output builder.

**Why each character is read once.** `j` moves forward through every character exactly once over the whole
loop, and `i` jumps straight to `j`.

build: Extend `j` to the end of the run.
Emit the character, and the length if above 1.

lines.text: An output builder and the start of the first run.

notes.c: The output is never longer than the input (a run of length ≥ 2 shrinks to the letter plus at most as many digits), so `n + 1` bytes are enough.

lines.text: Move `j` until the character changes; `j − i` is the run's length.
Write the character, plus its count only when the run is longer than 1.
The next run starts where this one ended.

complexity.md: **Time O(n).** **Space O(n)** for the output (at most `n` characters).

walk.title: Two pointers mark each run: i at its start, j moves until the character changes.

takeaways.md:
- **Runs of equal items:** a run-start pointer and a scanning pointer.
- Build strings with a builder, not repeated concatenation.
- **Pitfall:** writing single-digit counts only (`a12` needs two digits).
